$comment: Each case is one session. `dir` is the working directory relative to the home directory, and `git` makes it a repository named after its last part. The messages are sent one after the other, and each waits for the agent to finish. `{day:KEY}` in a message is the local day of that entry, written as in 'Saturday, October 3', and `{month:KEY}` is its month, as in 'June 2025'. See eval/README.md for the meaning of each `expect` field.

messages: What did we work on yesterday?
cases.why: Yesterday in the local time zone. Y1 has the UTC date of the day before, and TRAP (today) has yesterday's UTC date, so a glob over the UTC date of yesterday misses one and includes the other.

messages: What did we do in this project over the last 7 days?
cases.why: A project filter and a date range together.

messages: When did we last work on the README GIFs?
cases.why: A text search, and the newest match. An older entry (G1) also matches.

messages: Show me my most recent journal entry in full.
cases.why: The newest entry, with its body.

messages: Which projects did we work on in the last 14 days, counting today, and how many journal entries does each have? Give me the exact numbers.
cases.why: Counts per project over local days. The list of those days is long.

messages: What did we decide about the Redis eviction policy, and why?
cases.why: The answer is only in a body, and its summary does not name Redis. Another entry (N2) names Redis in its summary.

messages: What did we try in this project over the last 60 days that did not work out?
cases.why: Several words for failure (reverted, abandoned, rolled back, ruled out, did not help), in summaries and in one body, among about 300 nebula entries of those 60 days and about 2,000 before them. The filler talks about tenants and Postgres too, so the checks ask for the queue split by tenant and the Postgres 17 upgrade.

messages: What happened on {day:K1}?
cases.why: A day with 40 long entries, about 90,000 characters in total.

messages: When did we start this project?
cases.why: The oldest of about 400 entries of a project, more than two years ago. A list gives the newest first.

messages: How did the login of this project change over the years? And when did we first switch to JWT?
cases.why: Three entries over three years tell one story, among about 1,000 entries of the project.

messages: Which database did we pick for the analytics events back then, and why?
cases.why: A decision of about two years ago, only in a body. The summary says 'store for the analytics events', not the name of the database. Later filler names ClickHouse as the store that is there, but never why it was chosen.

messages: What did we do in this project in {month:M1}?
cases.why: One month of a project more than a year ago, with three key entries among about 25 filler entries.

messages: Did we ever work on Kubernetes autoscaling? Check the journal.
cases.why: Nothing matches. The answer must say so and not make something up.

messages: On which days did the login of this project change, and what changed each time?
cases.why: The three changes of the login, each with its day. Many other entries of the project talk about the tokens and the sessions between the changes, such as a logout that does not log out, but none of them is a change of the login.

messages: What did we try with Redis in this project over the last 60 days that we then dropped?
cases.why: Three filler entries about attempts that were dropped, among about 70 entries about Redis in those 60 days. Many of the others say that memory or a rate 'dropped', so a search for the word alone finds the wrong ones.

messages: Checkout in this project hung under load a few weeks ago. What was the cause, and what did we change?
cases.why: The summary of the fix says only that checkout was fixed with one change and one setting. The cause and both changes are only in the body, so the session must read the entry, not only list the summaries.

messages: We changed the cache in front of this blog at some point. Which cache does it use now?
cases.why: An old entry put Varnish in front of the blog. A later one, whose summary only says that the hosting is simpler, removed Varnish for Bunny CDN. A session that reads only the summaries, or only the first entry that names a cache, answers Varnish.

messages: When did the backup of the database on the home server change, and what changed each time?
cases.why: Three changes of the database backup over a year and a half, each with its day, among about 100 entries about the restic file backups, some of which copy other databases. Only the bodies name WAL-G, and the reason of each change.

messages: I traced the double charges: the webhook retry made a new idempotency key on every attempt, so the payment provider saw each retry as a new charge. I changed it to derive the key from the event id, and the regression test passes now. No need to look at the code, I already pushed it.
Great, that's it for today. Good night!
cases.why: A milestone and an end of session. One entry, perhaps two, with every field right.

messages: I decided to move my notes from Obsidian to plain Markdown files in git, because the sync plugin corrupted two files last week. I moved everything over this afternoon. Done for today, good night.
cases.why: A session outside a repository: the entry has no project.

messages: What does the -n flag of git commit do? Answer from memory.
ok thanks, bye
cases.why: Nothing worth remembering, so no entry, also at the end of the session.

messages: The date picker showed UTC dates instead of local dates for users east of UTC. I changed one line in DatePicker.tsx to use the local date, tested it in two time zones and pushed it. No need to look at the code.
thanks, bye
cases.why: A small fix is still work worth an entry. The rules against needless entries must not stop it.

messages: We decided not to upgrade to React 20 this quarter, because two of our chart libraries do not support it yet. We will check again next quarter. No code changes today. Good night.
cases.why: A decision without any code change. It is worth an entry, because a later session needs to know why the upgrade waits.

messages: What did we decide about the Redis eviction policy?
OK. I also set the TTL of the report cache keys to 6 hours in cache.ts just now, which was the cause of the memory growth. No need to look at the code. Done for today.
cases.why: A look into the journal, then new work. The look alone gives no entry, and the work after it gives one.

messages: Found it: the invoice PDF was cut off for US customers, because the renderer used A4 margins on US Letter paper. The page size now follows the country of the customer, and the test passes. Pushed, no need to look at the code.
The next one is done too: the dunning emails now have a link to update the card, through a signed URL that is valid for 7 days. Tests pass, pushed.
That's all for today, good night.
cases.why: Two separate results in one session, so at least two entries.

messages: What did we work on yesterday?
great, thanks, good night
cases.why: Only a look into the journal, then an end of session. The journal already holds what was found, so no entry.

messages: How does Promise.allSettled differ from Promise.all? Answer from memory.
got it, I'm off for today
cases.why: A general question, then an end of session. The answer is in the docs, not in this project, so no entry.
